pos.personaBrief: Flamengo pressed and, per Goal and Lance, dominated possession with enveloping touch play (6-2 Palmeiras), so it did not cede the ball to counter.

pro.personaBrief: Coutinho ordered recycling the ball back to the defense rather than aimless crosses, yet wanted fast kills after recovery and Andrade's long ball to Nunes won the final.

est.personaBrief: Coutinho brought sector-based organisation and polyvalence, with defined roles yet fluid overlapping fullbacks and Zico roaming behind the strikers.

lar.personaBrief: Wingers closed inside while fullbacks overlapped down the flank (Toninho scoring), and Zico played centrally behind the forwards, so a central focus with fullback width.

blo.personaBrief: High compact lines, pressing from the start and the aim of smothering opponents early (Lance 6-2, Trivela).

mar.personaBrief: Marcação por setor is credited to Coutinho, favouring spaces and sector responsibility over man-marking.

pla.personaBrief: Coutinho imposed a modern model of total participation, but also prepared the Atletico scheme for the final; the core identity stayed offensive.

res.personaBrief: Offensive, massacre-the-opponent approach: play to win, keep attacking, no settling for draws, with professional focus on results.

sis.personaBrief: Coutinho demanded total participation from everyone including strikers, while Zico was freed as the star; a drilled system around a genius.

jog.personaBrief: A technical team of Zico, Junior, Adilio and Carpegiani, with Cooper-method fitness and intensity as a base.

bas.personaBrief: Coutinho mixed the academy kids (Zico, Junior, Adilio, Andrade, Tita) with experienced players like Carpegiani, Raul and Toninho; the title was won with both.

lid.personaBrief: Coutinho was a professional, method-driven coach who gave orders and drilled fundamentals, while Bosco and Zico's leadership kept the group harmonious.
